Category.value: Recycled, recovered, or environmentally preferable materials

Statement.value: Recycled, recovered, environmentally preferable, or biobased materials should be used to the maximum extent possible, provided that the material meets or exceeds the operational and maintenance requirements, and promotes economically advantageous life cycle costs.
The materials and components shall conform to the requirements specified in material properties in accordance with the Quality Requirements and Inspections Methods.

Standard patterns, providing a seam allowance of ⅜ inch for all seams except where otherwise specified, will be furnished by the Government.  The list of pattern parts and computer nomenclature is provided to ensure that the pattern set provided is complete.  The Government patterns shall not be altered in any way, and shall only be used for cutting the contractor’s working patterns.  The working patterns shall be identical to the Government patterns, except that additional notching, if needed to facilitate manufacture is permitted on the contractor’s working pattern.  Minor modifications are permitted where necessary to accommodate the manufacturer’s processes and the use of automated equipment provided the modifications do not alter the dimensional, serviceability, or appearance requirements cited in this document or governed by the Government pattern.
Component parts shall be cut from the materials specified and in accordance with the pattern parts listed to achieve the desired fit.
The finished end item shall conform to the measurements specified in the Table of Finished Dimensions (TOFM) as defined by the Method of Measure (MOM).

All measurements are taken with garments laid on a flat, clean surface with all folds smooth, being careful not to stretch or distort the garment. All measurements are taken from the front of the garment unless otherwise noted.

End item construction shall conform to the requirements and figures  to maintain end item configuration as verified by the quality requirements and inspection methods specified.  Following the exact sequence of operations is not required, provided the finished end item meets the finished form, fit, and function requirements as those produced by following the sequence of operations.

The end item shall be made in accordance with the stitches and seams specified. The contractor is not required to follow a specific sequence of operations provided the finished end item meets the finished form, fit, and function.

The finished end item shall be uniform, and the occurrence of defects shall not exceed the established Acceptance Quality Limits (AQL) and shall not adversely affect the serviceability, appearance, and uniformity of the product.
Acquisition documents should specify the following acquisition requirements. See below:
This section contains information of a general or explanatory nature that may be helpful, but is not mandatory
Certificates of compliance may be accepted for selected requirements. It is recommended that vendors verify acceptability prior to using certificates of compliance to address requirements.

When first article inspection is required, the contracting officer should provide specific guidance to offerors whether the item(s) should be first article sample, a first production item, or a standard production item from the contractor’s current inventory, and the number of items to be tested. Invitations for bids should provide that the Government reserves the right to waive the requirement for samples for first article inspection to those bidders offering a product that has been previously acquired or tested by the Government and that bidders offering such products, who wish to rely on such production or test, must furnish evidence with the bid that prior Government approval is presently appropriate for pending contract. Bidders should not alternate submit bids unless specifically requested to do so in the solicitation.

For access to information such as specifications, drawings, and standard shade samples of cloth, go to https://www.dla.mil/TroopSupport/ClothingandTextiles/SpecRequest.aspx for DLA’s Troop Support’s Clothing and Textile Specification/Pattern/Drawing request form. Complete the request form and then submit the form. Request to use equivalent materials or components should be sent to the contracting officer for approval by the military service.

Samples shall be subjected to First Article inspection for compliance with design, configuration, workmanship, dimensional and testing requirements. First article  inspection shall consist of the inspection methods, examinations and tests specified.
The presence of defects exceeding AQLs specified in the contract  or failure of any testing (end item, material or component) shall be cause for rejection of the first article.
The sample size shall be as specified in the contract.  The sample unit shall be one finished end item and the lot size shall be expressed in units of end items.

Samples shall be subjected to Conformance inspections for compliance with design, configuration, workmanship, dimensional and testing requirements. Conformance inspection shall consist of the inspection methods, examinations and tests specified.
Acceptance quality limits (AQL) as specified in the contract and/or order, except where otherwise indicated.
Sampling for inspection shall be performed in accordance with ASQ/ANSI Z1.4.  The sample shall be one (1) end item and the lot size shall be expressed in units of end items.

Finished end items shall be inspected in accordance with the inspection methods specified and those referenced specifications and standards unless otherwise excluded, amended, or modified in this specification or applicable procurement documents
The end item shall be examined for defects in color, shade design, material, finish, construction, workmanship, marking, and the defects shall be classified in accordance with the list of defects.
The finished end item shall conform to the requirements listed when tested as specified.
The artwork shall conform to the requirements listed when examined as specified.
The label(s) shall conform to the requirements listed when examined as specified.
The finished end item shall be examined and scored for the defects listed.
Preservation, packing and marking shall be as specified in the contract.

For acquisition purposes, the packaging requirements shall be as specified in the contract or order.  When packaging of materiel is to be performed by DoD or in-house contractor personnel, these personnel need to contact the responsible packaging activity to ascertain packaging requirements.  Packaging requirements are maintained by the Inventory Control Point’s packaging activities within the Military Service or Defense Agency, or within the military service’s system commands.  Packaging data retrieval is available from the managing Military Department’s or Defense Agency’s automated packaging files, CD-ROM products, or by contacting the responsible packaging activity.
The end item(s) shall be in the following color(s) as specified in the contract.
